:::{#def-saturated-model}
#### Saturated model (full model, maximal model)

Consider a dataset with $q$ distinct covariate patterns $\vx_1, \ldots, \vx_q$,
and an outcome distribution family
(for example, Gaussian, Bernoulli, or Poisson).
The **saturated model** for that dataset and family
(also called the **full** or **maximal** model)
gives each distinct covariate pattern its own free mean parameter:

$$
\E{Y \mid \vX = \vx_k} \eqdef \mu_k,
\quad k = 1, \ldots, q,
$$

plus any dispersion parameter of the family
(such as $\sigma^2$ for the Gaussian family),
shared by all patterns
[@dobson4e, Chapter 5].

:::

::: notes
@def-saturated-model describes a model structure.
When the saturated model is fit by maximum likelihood
in the Gaussian, Bernoulli, or Poisson family,
the estimate $\est{\mu}_k$ is the sample mean of the outcomes
among the observations with pattern $\vx_k$,
so the saturated model reproduces every observed pattern mean exactly.
:::
